why: A script run by path puts its own folder first on the import path, so a file there named like a standard library module is what the script imports. The fail side tracks a scripts folder with a json module file next to a script that imports json. The pass side keeps that module inside a package folder with an __init__.py, the precision trade-off the rule makes. Stop judging Python file names and the fail side goes green; drop the package exemption and the pass side goes red.
